newsitem.title: UK: NWE low sulphur fuel falls hard on good avails.
newsitem.headline: NWE low sulphur fuel falls hard on good avails.

text.p: NWE low sulphur cracked fuel oil crashed as avails piled up in northwest Europe, more beckoned from the U.S., and Italian buying still appeared lacklustre, traders said.
Low sulphur swaps for January were around $5 a tonne weaker at $118 fob NWE and February paper traded at $119.
Holders of physical cargoes for January said they were unwilling to disclose any offer prices. "I am not making any offers in this market," one said. "I am just waiting for a bid."

Large avails were seen from across the Atlantic, and one dealer said he saw upwards of 100,000 tonnes of availabilities there for the end of January and the beginning of February. But said he did not know the prices at which these pieces would be available.
High sulphur barges were steady to firmer amid good bunker demand and after a utility bought a cargo on Tuesday, traders said.
High sulphur barges traded at $119 fob ARA and dealers said that the offer was at that level by the middle of the day.
High sulphur cargoes were little changed. A U.K. utility bought a 1.005 sg, 3.5 percent sulphur cargo, for delivery 5-20 days ahead, from a U.K.refiner. The cargo was traded at around $118.5 cif NWE.
